paragraphs: Lily's Diary, Saturday evening. Dear diary, Today was a great day, and I want to write it all down. This morning, the Explorers went to the pier for a sailing lesson. We took a bus at half past eight, and the sun was already hot. Teacher Kim came with us. I was a little nervous, because I could not swim very well.

At nine o'clock, we met the sailing teacher at the pier. He was a tall man with a blue cap and a friendly smile. He gave each of us a safety vest. "Always keep your vest on," he said. First, he showed us how to hold the sail. Mia and I sat in a small white boat with him. Leo and May shared another boat with Teacher Kim. The boat had no engine, only a big white sail.

I liked the wind best. Leo's boat went faster than ours, and Leo laughed a lot. Two white birds flew over the water. The boat moved quietly across the water. We had a conversation with the teacher about the wind. "Why does the boat go forward?" asked Mia. He explained, "The sail catches the wind and pushes the boat." I did not feel nervous anymore. I loved sailing together with my friends.

After dinner, I made a paper boat with Tom. Tom helped me make the paper boat in the right way. We filled the bathtub with water and put the boat in it. I blew gently, and the boat moved across the water. Pip sat on the floor and watched. He barked when the boat went round and round. He wanted the boat, but we did not let him have it. The floor was wet, and Mom gave us a towel. "Now you are a sailor," said Tom.

Tomorrow, I will write a paragraph for Explorers' Blog. It will include three photos from Mia. What do you like to do on the water? It was my first lesson, and I want many more. I hope that I can sail again next month. I am very tired, but I am also very happy. Good night, diary.
text.summary: In her diary, Lily writes about a Saturday sailing lesson with the Explorers at the pier. In the evening, she makes a paper boat with Tom and tries it in the bathtub while Pip watches.

Dear diary,
Today was a great day, and I want to write it all down.
This morning, the Explorers went to the pier for a sailing lesson.
We took a bus at half past eight, and the sun was already hot.
Teacher Kim came with us.
I was a little nervous, because I could not swim very well.
At nine o'clock, we met the sailing teacher at the pier.
He was a tall man with a blue cap and a friendly smile.
He gave each of us a safety vest.
"Always keep your vest on," he said.
First, he showed us how to hold the sail.
Mia and I sat in a small white boat with him.
Leo and May shared another boat with Teacher Kim.
The boat had no engine, only a big white sail.
I liked the wind best.
Leo's boat went faster than ours, and Leo laughed a lot.
Two white birds flew over the water.
The boat moved quietly across the water.
We had a conversation with the teacher about the wind.

He explained, "The sail catches the wind and pushes the boat."
I did not feel nervous anymore.
I loved sailing together with my friends.
After dinner, I made a paper boat with Tom.
Tom helped me make the paper boat in the right way.
We filled the bathtub with water and put the boat in it.
I blew gently, and the boat moved across the water.

The floor was wet, and Mom gave us a towel.
"Now you are a sailor," said Tom.
